correctness.rationale: Reconstructed all vertex and capacity inequalities for k-limited domination: a singleton shore cannot dominate omitted neighbors; any two vertices fail either chosen load or an omitted paired vertex. A three-vertex candidate with one L_i and two R vertices forces i>t and both opposite indices <=t; conversely each such configuration works and has selected outside-neighbor count n-2. The mirrored types exhaust |D|=3. Every 2+2 set works for |D|=4; at endpoint t=0,1,n no 1+3 can work and one-shore sets fail, so these are exactly all minima. An independent adjacency/bitset enumeration (not executing package checker) exhaustively confirmed every case n=3..8, all t (39 profiles), agreeing with both counts; universal conclusion follows from the case proof, not finite tests.

value.rationale: Edge removal can either decrease or increase the minimum under a fixed near-maximum local omission capacity, disproving both monotonicity intuitions for this natural nested graph family. Exact minimizer geometry/counts can be used as sharp test cases for nonregular limited domination bounds. The capacity n-2 has a structural role, not an arbitrary numerically selected slice.

final_claim: For G_{n,t}=K_{n,n} minus t disjoint matching edges at uniform capacity k=n-2, n>=3, the limited domination number is 3 for 2<=t<=n-1 and 4 for t=0,1,n; exact labeled minimizer counts are 2(n-t)C(t,2) and C(n,2)^2 respectively, with the complete types of minimum subsets.
